newsitem.title: USA: Edison sets meetings for power plant sale.
newsitem.headline: Edison sets meetings for power plant sale.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co said Monday it will conduct three pre-auction conferences for the divestiture of its natural gas-fueled power plants.

Edison also said its ownership share in the coal-fueled Mohave and Four Corners power plants in Nevada and New Mexico will be valued in line with California's requirements and a final decision about any sale of those plants will be made after more analysis.

As part of restructuring the state's electric utility industry, the California Public Utilities Commission required both Edison and Pacific Gas and Electric Co to divest at least 50 percent of their fossil-fueled generating plants.
Late last year, Edison announced plans to auction off 12 of its power plants, representing 100 percent of the utility's natural gas-fueled generation assets.
Edison will hold the pre-auction conferences on March 11 in Los Angeles, March 12 in Houston and March 13 in New York.

"(The conferences) are designed, in part, to create a level playing field for all interested parties by providing the same information to everyone at the same time," said Stephen Frank, SoCal Edison's president.
The 12 power plants to be auctioned are all located within Edison's California traditional service territory.
They have a total rated operating capacity of about 10,000 megawatts with a combined book value of about $700 million.
The utility will continue to own and operate its hydroelectric power facilities in California and its San Onofre nuclear power plant near San Clemente, Calif.
Edison also will continue to own a portion of the Palo Verde nuclear plant in Arizona.
